To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the thermal SZ effect toward Coma in four frequency bands, and the optical depth in the cluster center is τ = (4±1) × 10 ^{-3}.

we have measured the thermal SZ effect at 143, 214, and 272 GHz toward the Coma cluster of galaxies with an accuracy of 10%, and that the value we obtain for the optical depth τ = (4 ± 1) × 10 -3 is consistent with that derived from X-ray measurements.
we have detected the thermal SZ effect toward Coma at 143 GHz with a statistical significance of 4.7σ and have measured its value to be ΔT0 = (-179 ± 38) μK in the central region of the cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Sunya-ev-Zeldovich effect in clusters of galaxies.
the measurement and interpretation of the Sunyaew-Zeldovich effect in the Coma cluster of galaxies.

the development of new instrumentation and techniques for the study of the Sunyaeva-Zeldovich effect, which can be used to probe the thermal history of the intergalactic medium, and to measure the mass of galaxy clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal SZ effect has been detected at the 3.5σ level in the cluster center, and that the optical depth is consistent with the X-ray-derived value.
the SZ effect has been observed and measured in the Coma cluster with the expected amplitude and spatial variation.

the SZ effect has now been measured with a reasonable level of precision at three different frequencies in the same direction, and the results are consistent with the predictions of the thermal SZ theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the ability to measure the thermal SZ effect at millimeter wavelengths and to separate it from the much stronger atmospheric component, and have obtained an SZ measurement in good agreement with previous measurements.
the thermal SZ effect was detected at a high significance and that it is consistent with X-ray measurements.
we have measured the SZ effect in the Coma cluster with the highest signal-to-noise ratio to date.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SZ effect can be measured at millimeter wavelengths using drift-scanning techniques.
the SZ effect is a robust probe of the thermal properties of the hot intergalactic medium.
the thermal SZ effect can now be measured with a precision of 10-2 in a few hours of observation with a large telescope.
